summary: Hisatake Kato studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). A philosopher, he held posts at Yamagata University (~1970–1980), Tohoku University (~1989–1996), the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998), Tottori University of Environmental Studies (~2001–2007), and the University of Human Arts and Sciences (~2007–2011).

Hisayoshi Miyamoto, working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. He has held posts attested in 2026 at the Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hitoshi Inui, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held posts at Koyasan University (attested 1986 and 2015 as professor) and its Research Institute of Esoteric Buddhist Culture (attested 1992 as lecturer).

Hitoshi Katō, working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Japanology, held posts in 1992 at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Nara University of Education. He later served as professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

A linguist, Hla Pe studied at the University of Yangon (~1931–1938), University College London (~1938–1939), and SOAS (~1940–1944). At SOAS, he taught Burmese language and culture from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang, a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology, earned a PhD at the University of Washington (completed by 1994) under the doctoral supervision of Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Hogetsu (1737–1805) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Tsugen and Zuihe. He succeeded Tsugen and taught Hōkai.
Hoin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gyoin Hashimoto (~1952–1981) and at Ryukoku University (~1959–1963).
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University and KU Leuven, and taught Kyokuga Saeki.
Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts attested in 2026 at Minobusan University and the Eastern Institute.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Hojun Nagasaki studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1961–1964). He was a faculty member and later professor emeritus at Otani University (~1967–1999) and president of the Japanese Association for Jaina Studies in 1998.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Otani University and later served there as a professor (~1920–1944).
Hoko Kuwana, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and held a post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holly Gayley works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2002–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch, a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Harvard University (~1940–1957). He taught at Yale University (~1962–1963) and Harvard University (~1964–1981).

Hong Luo, who works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed doctoral studies at Peking University. He has held positions at the China Tibetology Research Center, Sichuan University as professor, and the University of Hamburg as research fellow (attested 2026).
Hongyue Guo, working in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied under Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Stephen R. Bokenkamp.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1963 and 1992), Minobusan University (attested 1996), and the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia at the University of Tokyo (attested 1996).
Hoong Teik Toh, working in Tibetology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, completed a PhD at Harvard University by 2004. He studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

A scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, Wales studied at Queens' College, Cambridge (BA, 1922) and SOAS (PhD, 1929–1931) under Charles Otto Blagden. He held posts at King's College Bangkok, Greater-India Research Committee, and Royal Asiatic Society (1964–1968).
